scenes.name: Grunge y rock alternativo
scenes.book: Heavy Metal: The Music and Its Culture
scenes.author: Deena Weinstein
scenes.desc: Nevermind de Nirvana (noviembre de 1991) llega al número uno el 11 de enero de 1992 y acaba con el reinado del lite metal. Los medios abrazan a Kurt Cobain y Eddie Vedder, las radios crean formatos «alternativos», la gran emisora de metal de Los Ángeles, KNAC, se vende en 1995 y MTV cancela Headbangers Ball en 1996; hasta Kerrang! se abre a la nueva moda, y los críticos, que crecieron con el rock universitario, ven por fin validado su gusto. El grunge no es metal aunque comparte la guitarra y la voz fuerte: alterna partes duras y suaves, canta el dolor y la desesperación, viste de tienda de segunda mano e identifica a la generación X con los débiles, frente al poder y el placer del metal («Somos pesados, pero no heavy metal», dice Krist Novoselic). Hacia 1998 el alternativo está moribundo.

scenes.name: Grunge
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El grunge, revival del hard rock de los setenta y renacimiento musical de Seattle, fue uno de los grandes fenómenos de los noventa (casi solo en EE UU). Green River lo inauguran (Come On Down) y Pearl Jam, Soundgarden, Melvins y Mudhoney fijan sus cuatro puntos cardinales; Nirvana, con Nevermind, lo convierten en una tragaperras y en la banda sonora de la crisis nerviosa de una generación. Después, Alice In Chains (Dirt), Foo Fighters, Hammerbox, GodHeadSilo, Everclear, Stone Temple Pilots, Tool (el grupo más innovador de la segunda generación: Aenima, Lateralus), God Machine, Helmet, Quicksand, Urge Overkill, los Smashing Pumpkins (Siamese Dream, Mellon Collie), Scarce, Creed, Bush, Manic Street Preachers, Silverchair.

podcast.title: Buzz Osborne's Recommendation to Nirvana (1990)
podcast.body: Buzz Osborne, a member of The Melvins and a figure "idolized by Kurt Cobain," played a pivotal role in Dave Grohl joining Nirvana. Osborne recommended Dave for the open drummer slot after Scream broke up, directly leading to Dave's audition and subsequent entry into Nirvana. "But then Buzz Osborne of the Melvins, a guy idolized by Kurt Cobain, recommended him for the open drummer slot with Nirvana."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Ultra-Deep Background on Dave Grohl: Part 2

podcast.title: Connecting Dave Grohl to Nirvana (1990)
podcast.body: Buzz Osborne, a member of the Seattle band The Melvins, played a crucial role in Dave Grohl joining Nirvana. When Grohl, a friend, called him desperate for a drumming gig, Osborne, aware of Nirvana's drummer issues, provided him with the phone number of Nirvana's bassist, directly leading to Grohl's audition and recruitment. "Now Buzz was in a Seattle band called The Melvins, and Dave was hoping that he knew of any openings for a drummer. Now it just so happens that one of Buzz's friends was having drummer issues. He gave Dave the bass player's phone number."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 5

podcast.title: Connections to Nirvana
podcast.body: The drummer for Melvins played drums on Nirvana's first demo. Buzz Osborne, Melvins' singer, introduced Dave Ball (who became Nirvana's drummer) to the other members of Nirvana. Melvins also frequently played concerts with Nirvana and members of Pearl Jam. "el batería de Melvin's fue el batería que tocó la batería en la primera maqueta de Irvana o por ejemplo Bussos Pong, que es el cantante de Melvin's fue el que introdujo a Dave Ball el que sería el batería de Irvana a los miembros de Irvana."

podcast.title: Early Grunge Pioneers
podcast.body: The Melvins were identified as one of the bands featured in the early years of grunge, specifically in the mid-1980s, contributing to the scene's foundational development. "In the early years, this would be the middle 1980s. It featured bands like the Melvin's..."

podcast.title: Early Grunge Sound
podcast.body: The Melvins, led by Buzz Osborne from Aberdeen, Washington, were featured on the 1985 "Deep Six" compilation, contributing some of the earliest sounds of grunge, arguably the most important alternative sound of the 1990s. "That's some of the earliest sounds of grunge, arguably the most important alternative sound of the 1990s. And it started in the local Seattle Indy scene."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Indie Rock: Part 3

podcast.title: Evolution of Style
podcast.body: Melvins evolved their style significantly around 1987, moving away from a thrash/hardcore sound. This evolution was influenced by the "rabioso" (furious) and introspective nature of Seattle bands, contrasting with the more "macarra" (thuggish) rock from places like Washington and California which were laying the groundwork for new punk bands like Blink-182 and Limp Bizkit. "Melvin se evolucionaron bastante su estilo a lo que sería su disco de 1987 porque abandonan ese estén a Tanis Lack Bang Harcord en la que estaba metido."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Cuál fue el primer disco de Grunge?

podcast.title: Influencing Kurt Cobain
podcast.body: Buzz Osborne and The Melvins were highly influential in the burgeoning Seattle scene, notably to Kurt Cobain of Nirvana, who was such a devoted fan that he would sometimes roadie for them without pay. "Nirvana, featuring of course Kurt Cobain, a stoner and former janitor who was such a big fan of the melvins that he's sometimes rowdy for them for free."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Alt-Rock: Chapter 11

podcast.title: Limited Influence on Alexis on Fire
podcast.body: While a heavy band, The Melvins were explicitly mentioned as a band that none of the Alexis on Fire members, except potentially Dallas Green, were listening to as an influence, highlighting specific sonic preferences even within heavy music. "None of us were listening to the Melvents. Right. You were listening to the Melvents, right?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Alexisonfire - In Their Own Words Podcast

podcast.title: Move to Seattle and Scene Integration
podcast.body: After forming, Melvins moved to Seattle and deeply integrated with the local music scene. This mixing with other bands was crucial for their stylistic evolution and connection to the emerging grunge sound. "cuando se vencia a Tel de Melvin's se mezcla muchísimo con todas las bandas locales y con ese video."

podcast.body: The Melvins, another influential band in the Pacific Northwest music scene, once opened for Bam Bam, highlighting Bam Bam's significance and presence within the early grunge community. "They had the melvins opened for them and get this."

xref.title: Dave Grohl Joined Nirvana Because His Band's Bassist Broke Up with His Girlfriend (1990)
xref.body: Dave dropped out of high school to tour with DC punk band Scream for about three years. In the summer of 1990, bassist Skeater Thompson flaked out mid-tour in Los Angeles over the loss of his girlfriend, canceling multiple shows. Dave was left penniless (temporarily crashing with three female mud wrestlers) and doing cash tiling work for food money. He called Melvins leader King Buzzo (Kurt Cobain's idol), whom he'd met in Europe, who told him Kurt had a band needing a drummer. Dave flew to Seattle on September 21, 1990; four days later he auditioned and passed. Dave later wrote a song about Skeater Thompson called "Just Another Story About Skeater Thompson," available only on a cassette-only release made under the name "Late" in late 1990, titled *Pocket Watch*. "Dave has never forgotten Skeater Thompson and how thankful he is that Skeater had such bad girlfriend trouble."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: 10 Unusual Things About Nirvana

xref.title: Dave Grohl's Audition and Joining (1990)
xref.body: After his previous band Scream disbanded, Dave Grohl was connected with Nirvana through Buzz Osborne of The Melvins. Grohl auditioned at the Dutchman rehearsal space in Seattle on September 25, 1990, and secured the drumming position instantly, completing the lineup that would become one of the most successful rock bands of the 1990s. "He auditioned at the Dutchman rehearsal space in Seattle on September 25th, 1990, and he got the gig instantly."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 5

xref.title: Joining Nirvana (1990)
xref.body: A few months after recording his Harling Talks AD demos, Dave Grohl received a call to audition for Nirvana. Scream had broken up over "girlfriend troubles" while on tour, leaving Dave stranded in Los Angeles. Buzz Osborne of The Melvins, who was idolized by Kurt Cobain, recommended Dave for the open drummer position. Dave flew to Seattle, arriving on Friday, September 21, 1990, and after an informal audition, became a member of the band without any explicit invitation, simply because "they just didn't ask him to leave." "Dave packed his kit into a large cardboard box and boarded a flight for Seattle, arriving on Friday, September 21, 1990."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Ultra-Deep Background on Dave Grohl: Part 2

xref.title: Dave Grohl's Entrance – A Desperate Call
xref.body: After his band Scream broke up mid-tour in September 1990, Dave Grohl was stranded in Los Angeles and desperate for a gig. He called his friend Buzz Osborne of The Melvins, hoping for news of drummer openings. Osborne gave Grohl Kurt Cobain's phone number, leading to an invitation to Seattle. Grohl packed his drums in a cardboard box and joined Nirvana. "So buzz gave Dave the bass player his phone number and Dave made the call and was invited to come on up Packed all his drums into a big cardboard box grabbed his only bag close and headed up the coast to join this weird little band called of course Nirvana."

xref.title: First Subpop Singles Club Release
xref.body: Nirvana, an obscure trio from Aberdeen, Washington (the same town as The Melvins), was the artist featured on the very first limited edition single sent to subscribers of the Subpop Singles Club in November 1988. "The very first single of the month started arriving in mailboxes in November of 1988. It was from this obscure trio from a tiny logging town called Aberdeen, Washington, the same place as the Melvins. And they were called Nirvana."

xref.title: Lack of Recognition
xref.body: Despite playing important gigs and festivals, recording at the same studio as Nirvana's first records, winning local music awards, having The Melvins open for them, and even featuring Kurt Cobain at one point, Bam Bam and Tina Bell are almost completely omitted from the history of grunge. Existing online mentions are often incorrect or omit Tina entirely. "But they're almost completely expunged from the history of Grunge."

xref.title: Pioneering Recording at Reciprocal Recording
xref.body: Bam Bam made their first record, the "Villains" EP, in 1984 at Reciprocal Recording. This made them the first Grunge band to record at that studio, which later became famous for hosting bands like Nirvana, Alice in Chains, Soundgarden, The Melvins, and Mudhoney. "They used reciprocal recording, making them the first Grunge band to make music there."

xref.body: Despite their obscurity, BamBam played important gigs and festivals, recorded at the same studio where Nirvana made their first records, won local music awards, and even had The Melvins open for them. xref.title: Speculation on Undied Life
xref.body: If Kurt had not died, it is speculated that he would have separated from Nirvana for a solo project with different musicians, possibly Buzz Osborne of the Melvins and Michael Stipe of R.E.M., with whom he had discussed working. This solo record would likely have had a more acoustic feel with string arrangements. "Well my guess would be that he would have separated himself from Nirvana for his next project using different musicians. Maybe people like, I don't know, Buzz A's, One of the Melvin's and most likely Michael Stipe of R.E.M."
